findings.summary: The Deterministic preset now starts on Jolt (strict-FP build, physics.deterministic on) although triggers, layers, contact/trigger events and queries are silently absent (one warning only); nothing in the validation refuses or flags it
findings.scenario: A Deterministic lockstep project that relies on OnTriggerEnter or a layer matrix starts cleanly on the GCC strict build and plays with no triggers, no events and every layer colliding; the dev recorded it as a FINDING, the user must accept it or the check should refuse until J4/J5

findings.summary: The Jolt section's 'Not verified' callout lists 'that the hashes of all legs are equal', but JoltBackendDeterminismTest asserts the golden constants on every leg and docs/testing.html tabulates equal hashes on all seven legs
findings.scenario: A reader of physics.html is told cross-leg equality is unverified while the CI test fails on any leg that differs; the two docs pages contradict each other

findings.summary: In a build with N2ENGINE_USE_JOLT=ON and N2ENGINE_USE_PHYSX=OFF (the GCC strict leg's configuration), a project that does not set physics.backend gets no physics ('Built without PhysX') even though Jolt is compiled in: the default/fallback is always PhysX
findings.scenario: Jolt-only build, project without physics.backend: physicsStatus Disabled, every Rigidbody logs 'Physics backend not available'; only an explicit physics.backend jolt gets the Jolt backend (pre-existing ChooseBackend rule, now reachable)
